data.title: The Christmas Lights
data.rumour: Somebody's bought every string of Christmas lights in town. In October. Paid cash.
about: An October romance. Nolan Treadwell of the light company is buying every string of Christmas lights in town, and you find Odile's 1958 bubble lights under the counter (§{lightsNolan}). Lend them, sell them to him, or say you have none. He explains: Annika, who works nights in Hyannis, has only ever seen the town in the dark, so he's going to light up the Green for her. A Christmas-shop owner, Opal Sandeman, also wants the bubble lights (§{lightsOpal}).

On the Green that night (§{lightsGreen}) you hold the ladder, watch for her car, or film it from behind the war memorial. If Odile's lights are there they fill the gap in the middle, and the message reads WILL YOU MARRY ME with nine bubbling candles (Bubble Lights). Without them Nolan runs out of R, and it reads WILL YOU MARY ME; she says yes anyway (Will You Mary Me).

bubbleLights.name: Odile's 1958 bubble lights
tells: A string of nine glass candles. Plug them in and the liquid inside bubbles, eventually.
The box says NOMA in red and XMAS - O. in Odile's marker.

overheard.line: Puzzled: "Somebody's bought every string of Christmas lights in town. In October. Hal Mayhew says he paid cash and wore sunglasses."

lightsNolan.title: Nolan wants every Christmas light in town

text: Nolan Treadwell, Hollow Neck Light and Power. Do you have Christmas lights? Any. I've bought every string in Mayhew's. And the CVS. And the church's.

steps.narrate: Under the counter, behind the receipt books, is a box marked XMAS - O. in Odile's marker: a string of glass bubble lights from 1958.

choose.label: Lend them to him for the night

then.why: Sold Odile's bubble lights to Nolan Treadwell

steps.text: No? Okay. I'll drive to Hyannis.

text: Can I tell you why? You can't tell anyone. Annika works nights at the hospital in Hyannis. Two years. She's only ever seen this town in the dark, on her way home.
So {placed:lights-green} night I'm lighting up the Green. Every string I could find. Spelling something. You should come. Bring a thermos.

steps.toast: Calendar: something on the Green, {placed:lights-green} night

lightsOpal.title: Opal Sandeman wants the bubble lights

steps.text: Opal Sandeman. I run Christmas in Chatham, all year round, it's a whole thing. Hal Mayhew says you've got NOMA bubble lights. The 1958 ones.

then.text: Gone? To a lineman? For a WHAT? Oh, that's lovely. That's terrible. Lovely.
Lent out till after the weekend? Well, if they come back in one piece, I'll give you {hook:opalPrice}. Bubble lights never come back in one piece.

then.with: Sold Odile's bubble lights to Opal Sandeman

then.text: They're going in the front window. On a tree. In October. With all the others.
You're sentimental. I respect it. I've got a card.

steps.narrate: Harbor Green, eleven at night. Every string of lights in Hollow Neck is laid out across the grass in letters ten feet tall, running back to one orange extension cord and a generator from Light and Power.

steps.text: Hold this. Don't plug it in. Don't let me plug it in. She's off at eleven-thirty and she drives past the Green to get home.

narrate.then: In the middle of it, where a heart would be, he's laid Odile's bubble lights in a circle.
narrate.else: You walk the letters with him. W, I, L, L, Y, O, U, M, A, R, Y, M, E. You count them twice.

choose.label: Watch the road for her headlights
Hide behind the war memorial with his phone, filming

then.narrate: You crouch behind the war memorial. The names of every Hollow Neck man lost at sea since 1851 are very close to your face. It feels like the right audience.

steps.narrate: Headlights. A small car slows, stops. A woman in scrubs and a puffer jacket gets out and stands at the edge of the grass, in the dark.

then.narrate: The whole Green lights up: WILL YOU MARRY ME, in every color Mayhew's sells. In the middle, nine glass candles start, one after another, to bubble.

then.text: Oh. Oh, Nolan. Is this what it looks like? The town? Is this what it looks like in the light?
No. It's much worse. Will you?
Yes. Yes. Turn it off before the neighbors call it in.
Your lights. Every bulb. I counted. Thank you.

else.narrate: The whole Green lights up, in every color Mayhew's sells: WILL YOU MARY ME.

else.text: I ran out of R. There's no R left in this town. I checked the church.
Yes. Obviously yes. I'm calling you Mary from now on.

epilogue.line: Nolan and Annika are getting married in December, on the Green, at night. Odile's bubble lights are invited.
Annika Soule calls her fiance Mary. So does all of Hollow Neck Light and Power.
